title: AI guys beefing with the pope: A brief recap
key_facts: PC Gamer's column recaps an ongoing argument between AI supporters and the pope over whether AI is compatible with religious belief and whether making a computer talk creates life.
PC Gamer says a New York Times report published this week found that Anthropic lobbied the pope's advisers in May to take the idea of AI model consciousness seriously.
The pope's earlier letter, Magnifica Humanitas, said AI does not undergo experiences, have a body, feel joy or pain, or know from within what love, work, friendship or responsibility mean.
Former White House technology adviser Dean Ball criticized the letter, saying it puts the Church in the 'awkward role of the European technocratic regulatory advocate'.

This week the pope posted an 'anti-slop' message on X saying it is urgent to tell human art from what machines produce and that the Church wants to renew an alliance with artists and cultural institutions.
PC Gamer says there is a lot of support for the pope's stance on X, as well as AI supporters pushing back; it is a light-hearted opinion piece.
quote_evidence: According to a New York Times report published this week, Anthropic lobbied the pope's advisers "to take the prospect of AI model consciousness seriously" back in May.
it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce
Algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
why_it_matters_hint: A major religious leader is publicly taking a side on AI art and AI consciousness, and AI companies are reportedly lobbying him.
event_date: Week of 2 Oct 2026 (pope's X post, NYT report); the lobbying was 'back in May' (year not stated).
notes: Opinion and satire column. The Anthropic lobbying claim is PC Gamer relaying the New York Times; the Times piece was not read. The pope's name is not given in the article.
